key_insight: Large action spaces make contextual bandit learning fragile, so the paper reduces complexity by sharing structure across actions and by using pessimistic, optimizable objectives for logged-data learning.
engineering_relevance: These methods improve decision-making in high-dimensional control, recommendation, and adaptive optimization systems where only sparse feedback or offline logs are available.
method: On-policy: structured Bayesian exploration via meTS (mixed effects) and dTS (diffusion-inspired priors) to transfer information across actions.
Off-policy: sDM latent-variable direct modeling plus concave policy-weighted log-likelihood objectives for efficient optimization.
Pessimistic learning: differentiable exponential-smoothing and PAC-Bayesian regularization to balance bias and variance in importance-sampling estimators.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports regret guarantees for the on-policy methods and highlights that in large action spaces optimization error can dominate estimation error for off-policy learning.
watch_item: Performance depends on how well the chosen action structure or latent assumptions match the true problem; otherwise shared priors and pessimistic regularization may bias learning.
paper_title: On-Policy and Off-Policy Learning for Large Action Spaces
